## Exact observed failure

The first fixture reached preview, sharp safe, sharp strict, sharp transform and
viewport rotation with actual pixel checks. At the later direct
`logic.photoViewController.updateMultiple(scale: 1, rotation: 0, ...)` reset,
PhotoView reported twice:

```text
A IgnorableValueNotifier<PhotoViewScaleState> was used after being disposed.
PhotoViewScaleStateController.setInvisibly
PhotoViewControllerDelegate._blindScaleListener
PhotoViewController.updateMultiple
```

The next frame's existing `takeException == null` assertion failed. No color,
alpha, orientation or error tolerance was changed, and no exception was ignored.
The first run therefore does **not** establish the remaining F4 matrix cells.

## Static evidence and proposed minimal investigation scope

The dependency revision used by the project is
`photo_view-a1255d1b5945aad4b7323303ec2ecdf0c90ffc4c`.
Its `PhotoViewControllerDelegate.initDelegate` adds a `_blindScaleListener` to
an externally supplied `PhotoViewController` and a listener to its scale-state
controller. Its `dispose` removes only the latter listener. The retained
controller can therefore still notify an old delegate, which calls
`scaleStateController.setInvisibly` on its retired scale-state controller.

The reader's [controller lookup](<../../../lib/pages/reader/reading_logic.dart#L142-L148>)
retains a controller by page index. Switching preview/sharp replaces PhotoView
subtrees while retaining that controller. This is a plausible deterministic
controller-listener lifecycle issue exposed by the new combined sequence, not
proof of a format decoder defect or the user's original field incident.

The minimal investigation surface is dependency controller-listener retirement
or reader mode/controller generation handling. Neither dependency nor production
was modified. Main was notified before any proposed adjustment to separate
fresh-route transform coverage from same-session quality/mode-switch coverage.
Any subsequent narrower passing quality run must keep this failure record and
must not claim the combined lifecycle issue was repaired.
